THEOREMS

Proved from runs of the theories, not written by hand. The theory is a dropdown on each title - it is what changes which rules ran, and the same derivation usually survives the change with different numbers in it. The lattice is a setting below that; where lattices genuinely disagree the results are separate and have arrows between them. Click a line to see the working.

atom.hydrogen

one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?

the runs, and what they measured

gravity.full

put the pieces together. What is the gravitational force between two bodies R apart, with every factor written in?

reached on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2 - 4 lattices, G, dense regime - there are partners everywhere, so the hand-off is never what a carrier waits for and the lattice's one-cell-a-tick is the binding bound

reached on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2 - 4 lattices, G, thin regime - partners are scarce, so a carrier waits for one and the hand-off rate is the binding bound - which is what makes the speed follow the density

the runs, and what they measured

met.integral

reached on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2 - 4 lattices, G, dense regime - there are partners everywhere, so the hand-off is never what a carrier waits for and the lattice's one-cell-a-tick is the binding bound

reached on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2 - 4 lattices, G, thin regime - partners are scarce, so a carrier waits for one and the hand-off rate is the binding bound - which is what makes the speed follow the density

reached on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2 - 4 lattices, G, dense regime - there are partners everywhere, so the hand-off is never what a carrier waits for and the lattice's one-cell-a-tick is the binding bound

the runs, and what they measured

one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?
G^XOR on fcc-12, cubic-6
premise
E·r is the same on every shell

and the same numbers read as an energy rather than as a balance: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so E·r is the coupling again up to a factor that is the same on every shell. Measured, it moves by 0.00 per cent across n = 1 to 4. It is NOT a second measurement - it is the first one read the other way, and saying so is the difference between two premises and one premise counted twice

E·r = -0.0313
definition
E·r = En · rn

and the same coupling read as an energy: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so an energy times a radius is that coupling again up to a factor which is also the same on every shell. This is not a second premise - it is the first one written the other way, which is why the run reports one measurement behind both

balancing a conserved product
En ∝ 1rn
E·r = En · rn = constant
En·rn = constant
En1 ∝ 1 / (rn)
En ∝ 1rn

E·r cannot change, and written out it is En·rn. En carries the exponent 1 there, so holding the product fixed pins En to the rest raised to -1

premise
p2r is the same on every shell

what holds a thing in a circle is its momentum against the pull, and the pull here is the sign law's coupling over r2 - so p2/r = gq/r2 and p2r is the coupling itself. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES AND OF NOTHING ELSE, so it cannot depend on which shell is being asked about - measured across the four lowest, it moves by 0.00 per cent

p2r = 0.0625; E·r = -0.0313
definition
p2r = p · p · rn

and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. What keeps a thing on a curve goes as p2/r and what pulls it goes as gq/r2 - charge.attraction's coupling over charge.falloff's room - so setting the two equal leaves p2r = gq, with the inverse square already divided out. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES, so it is the same on every shell, and the run measured that rather than assuming it

definition
p ∝ nrn

matter.debroglie established that a region holds a whole number of nodes and that this comes to p·r = n·pi·hbar. Neither pi nor hbar has anything to do with which shell is being asked about, so as a statement about how the momentum moves when the shell does, it is p ∝ n/r. The constants are not lost - they are in the line that is cited, and they set the SIZE of the atom rather than the shape of the ladder

balancing a conserved product
rn ∝ n2
p2r = p · p · rn = constant
n2rn = constant
rn-1 ∝ 1 / (n2)
rn ∝ n2

p2r cannot change, and written out it is nodes2rn. rn carries the exponent -1 there - it appears more than once, because the factors are not all independent of it, so holding the product fixed pins rn to the rest raised to 1

expansion
En ∝ 1n2

rn is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?

matter.debroglie established that a region holds a whole number of nodes and that this comes to p·r = n·pi·hbar. Neither pi nor hbar has anything to do with which shell is being asked about, so as a statement about how the momentum moves when the shell does, it is p ∝ n/r. The constants are not lost - they are in the line that is cited, and they set the SIZE of the atom rather than the shape of the ladder

balancing a conserved product
rn ∝ n2
p2r = p · p · rn = constant
n2rn = constant
rn-1 ∝ 1 / (n2)
rn ∝ n2

p2r cannot change, and written out it is nodes2rn. rn carries the exponent -1 there - it appears more than once, because the factors are not all independent of it, so holding the product fixed pins rn to the rest raised to 1

expansion
En ∝ 1n2

rn is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?
G^XOR+XOR on square-4, line-2
one body biased one way, one the other. The sign law says what they pull with and the counting condition says what can stand in it - so how far out are the shells, and what does it take to get off one?
G^XOR^o on fcc-12, cubic-6
premise
E·r is the same on every shell

and the same numbers read as an energy rather than as a balance: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so E·r is the coupling again up to a factor that is the same on every shell. Measured, it moves by 0.00 per cent across n = 1 to 4. It is NOT a second measurement - it is the first one read the other way, and saying so is the difference between two premises and one premise counted twice

E·r = -0.0313
definition
E·r = En · rn

and the same coupling read as an energy: what is not kinetic is potential, the potential is the coupling over r, so an energy times a radius is that coupling again up to a factor which is also the same on every shell. This is not a second premise - it is the first one written the other way, which is why the run reports one measurement behind both

balancing a conserved product
En ∝ 1rn
E·r = En · rn = constant
En·rn = constant
En1 ∝ 1 / (rn)
En ∝ 1rn

E·r cannot change, and written out it is En·rn. En carries the exponent 1 there, so holding the product fixed pins En to the rest raised to -1

premise
p2r is the same on every shell

what holds a thing in a circle is its momentum against the pull, and the pull here is the sign law's coupling over r2 - so p2/r = gq/r2 and p2r is the coupling itself. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES AND OF NOTHING ELSE, so it cannot depend on which shell is being asked about - measured across the four lowest, it moves by 0.00 per cent

p2r = 0.0625; E·r = -0.0313
definition
p2r = p · p · rn

and what the balance holds fixed is momentum twice and radius once. What keeps a thing on a curve goes as p2/r and what pulls it goes as gq/r2 - charge.attraction's coupling over charge.falloff's room - so setting the two equal leaves p2r = gq, with the inverse square already divided out. THE COUPLING IS A PROPERTY OF THE TWO BODIES' BIASES, so it is the same on every shell, and the run measured that rather than assuming it

G^XOR · relaxing(2/1) on square-4, line-2
the half in the gravitational constant is how often two charges are opposed, and that is a fact about the bodies rather than a number. What happens to the force when they are biased?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
F = Fvac + Fq

and what a body actually feels is everything that arrives, which is BOTH channels - and only one of them has been touched. The vacuum channel needs neither body to emit anything: a body's cells are not neutral, the split does not fire on them, and the expansion that did not happen spreads outward as a shortfall whatever signs anybody is carrying. THERE IS NOTHING IN IT FOR A BIAS TO ACT ON, so it is the same for both signs of charge and cannot be screened by either. That is the part of this law that is gravity, and it is why a charged thing falls like an uncharged one even where the other channel is pulling it about

definition
Fq = Fmeet · gq

and a pair that meets opposed that fraction as often feels that fraction of the meeting channel. This line says nothing except what a ratio is

definition
gq = opposedshare

gravity.full writes the meeting channel as six factors multiplied - what one meeting is worth to a path, how much of the time the two are OPPOSED, the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, the two masses, and the meetings summed along the line. Exactly one of those asks about the SIGNS the bodies are carrying, and it is the second: the rest are counts of the tiling, masses, and a distance, and not one of them moves when a body is biased. So the biased and unbiased channels differ by that factor alone and everything else cancels out of the ratio

as a ratio
gq = opposedshare

gq is opposed over share, which written out is opposedshare - kept in the counts rather than worked out, so that whatever uses it can cancel against them

substituting
Fq = Fmeet·opposedshare
Fq = Fmeet·gq
gq = opposedshare
Fq = Fmeet·opposedshare

gq is not a primitive of this theory - it is opposedshare, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
share = noppnstates

two charges are opposed exactly when their meeting leaves nothing - that is what the word means for a rule that either annihilates a pair or does not. The states a pair can be in are equally available, so how much of the time they are opposed is how many of those states annihilate, over how many there are

premise
nopp = 1

and left nothing at all in the other 1: those are the states in which the two were opposed, which is what being opposed MEANS in a theory whose meetings either annihilate a pair or do not

surviving = 0
a number is an expression
nopp = 1

annihilating is 1, so it can stand in an expression as that

premise
nstates = 1

a ray of G can be carrying nothing but itself, so a facing pair has 1 possible states and the enumeration is complete

cases = 1
a number is an expression
nstates = 1

cases is 1, so it can stand in an expression as that

one over another
share = 1
share = nopp / nstates
= (1) / (1)
= 1

annihilating is 1 and cases is 1, so the one over the other is 1

substituting
Fq = Fmeet·opposed
Fq = Fmeet·opposedshare
share = 1
Fq = Fmeet·opposed

share is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

F = Fq + Fvac

definition
gq = opposedshare

gravity.full writes the meeting channel as six factors multiplied - what one meeting is worth to a path, how much of the time the two are OPPOSED, the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, the two masses, and the meetings summed along the line. premise
opposed = 1 - Pa·Pb2

ANNIHILATION leaves nothing exactly when the pair is opposite - enumerated over a real facing pair, - with -: both still there; - with +: nothing left; + with -: nothing left; + with +: both still there - so how often two bodies meet opposed is how often one offers a + while the other offers a -, either way round. At biases Pa and Pb that is (1+Pa)(1-Pb)/4 + (1-Pa)(1+Pb)/4, which multiplies out to (1 - Pa·Pb)/2 - exactly, over all 49 bias pairs, to 0.000000. And the 1254 meetings actually run at the corners and the middle agree with it to 0.0440 against a sampling error of 0.0316. NOTE WHAT IS NOT ASSUMED: not that the rule destroys the opposite pairs, which was enumerated; and not that the two draws are independent, which is what drawing them from two bodies makes true

bias pairs worked out = 49; worst |worked out - (1 - Pa·Pb)/2| = 0.0000; meetings actually run = 1254; worst |run - (1 - Pa·Pb)/2| = 0.0440
definition
share = noppnstates

as a ratio
share = noppnstates

share is annihilating over cases, which written out is annihilatingcases - kept in the counts rather than worked out, so that whatever uses it can cancel against them

one over another
gq = 1 - Pa·Pb
gq = opposed / share
= (1/2 - 1/2·Pa·Pb) / (noppnstates)
= 1 - Pa·Pb

opposed is 1/2 - 1/2·Pa·Pb and share is annihilatingcases, so the one over the other is 1 - Pa·Pb

And the 1254 meetings actually run at the corners and the middle agree with it to 0.0440 against a sampling error of 0.0316. NOTE WHAT IS NOT ASSUMED: not that the rule destroys the opposite pairs, which was enumerated; and not that the two draws are independent, which is what drawing them from two bodies makes true

bias pairs worked out = 49; worst |worked out - (1 - Pa·Pb)/2| = 0.0000; meetings actually run = 1254; worst |run - (1 - Pa·Pb)/2| = 0.0440
definition
share = noppnstates

two charges are opposed exactly when their meeting leaves nothing - that is what the word means for a rule that either annihilates a pair or does not. The states a pair can be in are equally available, so how much of the time they are opposed is how many of those states annihilate, over how many there are

as a ratio
share = noppnstates

share is annihilating over cases, which written out is annihilatingcases - kept in the counts rather than worked out, so that whatever uses it can cancel against them

one over another
gq = 1 - Pa·Pb
gq = opposed / share
= (1/2 - 1/2·Pa·Pb) / (noppnstates)
= 1 - Pa·Pb

opposed is 1/2 - 1/2·Pa·Pb and share is annihilatingcases, so the one over the other is 1 - Pa·Pb

substituting
F = Fmeet - Fmeet·Pa·Pb + Fvac
F = Fmeet·gq + Fvac
gq = 1 - Pa·Pb
F = Fmeet - Fmeet·Pa·Pb + Fvac

gq is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 - Pa·Pb, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

the half in the gravitational constant is how often two charges are opposed, and that is a fact about the bodies rather than a number. What happens to the force when they are biased?
G^XOR · relaxing(2/1) on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
F = Fvac + Fq

and what a body actually feels is everything that arrives, which is BOTH channels - and only one of them has been touched. The vacuum channel needs neither body to emit anything: a body's cells are not neutral, the split does not fire on them, and the expansion that did not happen spreads outward as a shortfall whatever signs anybody is carrying. THERE IS NOTHING IN IT FOR A BIAS TO ACT ON, so it is the same for both signs of charge and cannot be screened by either. That is the part of this law that is gravity, and it is why a charged thing falls like an uncharged one even where the other channel is pulling it about

and a pair that meets opposed that fraction as often feels that fraction of the meeting channel. This line says nothing except what a ratio is

F = Fq + Fvac
Fq = Fmeet·gq
F = Fmeet·gq + Fvac

definition
gq = opposedshare

gravity.full writes the meeting channel as six factors multiplied - what one meeting is worth to a path, how much of the time the two are OPPOSED, the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, the two masses, and the meetings summed along the line. Exactly one of those asks about the SIGNS the bodies are carrying, and it is the second: the rest are counts of the tiling, masses, and a distance, and not one of them moves when a body is biased. So the biased and unbiased channels differ by that factor alone and everything else cancels out of the ratio

a charge's field falls off as one over the square of the distance. How much of it is left beyond a radius r?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
ε = ∫∞r 1/s2 ds

everything past r is everything at every s from r outwards, added up - and there is no outer edge to stop at, so the upper limit is however far you care to go

definition
1/s2 = 1s2

what a charge leaves at a distance falls off as one over the square of it - which is gravity.falloff at D = 3, cited rather than counted again

integrating a power
ε = 1r
ε = ∫Infinityr 1s2 ds
= s-1-1, at the limits
= 1r

what is at s is 1s2, a power -2 of s. Integrated that is s-1/-1, taken between r and Infinity

the rays carry a sign, transport keeps it, and a round source puts out a net of it. How much of it is at one site, a distance away?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
the rays carry a sign, transport keeps it, and a round source puts out a net of it. How much of it is at one site, a distance away?
G^XOR on square-4, line-2
premise
q is conserved in flight

run with MOVEMENT and ARRIVAL and nothing else, the multiset of what the rays are carrying as polarity is exactly what it was 6 ticks earlier. Transport writes each ray's contents onto one neighbour and swaps them in, and polarity is part of what a ray carries - so it is moved and neither made nor unmade. Compared as a MULTISET rather than as a sum, so a rule that swapped two rays' labels would be caught rather than counted as conservative. This holds at every shell at once and for every run length, because it is a property of the rule. Set aside to ask it: EMISSION, CREATION, ANNIHILATION, TRANSPORT

polarity, carried = 84
premise
q goes every way alike

handed a source with no axis, GXOR's own EMISSION rule wrote the same value of polarity on every one of its 6 exits - not most of them, all of them. So what a round source puts out goes every way alike, which is what says a share is the whole of it over the WHOLE shell rather than over some part of it

polarity over the exits of a round source = 6
spreading
n[q] ∝ qshell

conserved and even, so one site's share is the whole of it over the number of sites there are at that distance

premise
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)

a site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the sites at exactly r steps are those within r less those within r-1 - a subtraction, with nothing left over and nothing counted twice

sites within r steps = 8
premise
ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
ball(r) = 1, 5, 13, 25, 41, 61, 85, 113, 145
Δ1 = 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32
Δ2 = 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4

the sites within r steps are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step - take one step r times and you are somewhere in r·P, and every site of r·P is reached that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 2, which is D, exactly and on integers

sites within r steps = 8; degree of the count in r = 2
Ehrhart's theorem
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD
ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
= β·rD + c1·rD-1 + ... + cD
∝ β·rD

Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality

the difference of a dilate
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)
= β·rD - β·(r-1)D
= β·rD - β·(rD - D·rD-1 + ...)
= β·D·rD-1 + ...
∝ β·rD-1

every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

expansion
n[q] ∝ qSTEP·rD-1

shell is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

the sites within r steps are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step - take one step r times and you are somewhere in r·P, and every site of r·P is reached that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 2, which is D, exactly and on integers

sites within r steps = 8; degree of the count in r = 2
Ehrhart's theorem
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD
ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
= β·rD + c1·rD-1 + ... + cD
∝ β·rD

Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality

the difference of a dilate
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)
= β·rD - β·(r-1)D
= β·rD - β·(rD - D·rD-1 + ...)
= β·D·rD-1 + ...
∝ β·rD-1

every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

the sites within r steps of a source spanning 1 direction are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step of it, in the 1 directions ACROSS it - the source already spans the other 1, so nothing grows that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 1, which is D-1, exactly and on integers

sites within r of a 1-dimensional source = 41; degree of that count in r = 1
Ehrhart's theorem
ball about a 1-dimensional source(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
ball about a 1-dimensional source(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
= β·rD-1 + c1·rD-1-1 + ... + cD-1
∝ β·rD-1

Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D-1 and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality

the difference of a dilate
shell about a wire(r) ∝ STEP·rD-2
shell about a wire(r) = ball about a 1-dimensional source(r) - ball about a 1-dimensional source(r-1)
= β·rD - β·(r-1)D
= β·rD - β·(rD - D·rD-1 + ...)
= β·D·rD-1 + ...
∝ β·rD-1

every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

premise
q is conserved in flight

run with MOVEMENT and ARRIVAL and nothing else, the multiset of what the rays are carrying as polarity is exactly what it was 6 ticks earlier. Transport writes each ray's contents onto one neighbour and swaps them in, and polarity is part of what a ray carries - so it is moved and neither made nor unmade. Compared as a MULTISET rather than as a sum, so a rule that swapped two rays' labels would be caught rather than counted as conservative. This holds at every shell at once and for every run length, because it is a property of the rule. Set aside to ask it: EMISSION, CREATION, ANNIHILATION, TRANSPORT, RELAXATION

polarity, carried = 84
premise
q goes every way alike

handed a source with no axis, GXOR · relaxing(2/1)'s own EMISSION rule wrote the same value of polarity on every one of its 6 exits - not most of them, all of them. So what a round source puts out goes every way alike, which is what says a share is the whole of it over the WHOLE shell rather than over some part of it

polarity over the exits of a round source = 6

the record is left anywhere on the shell, not at one chosen place - so the rate over the whole field is the rate at one place times how many places there are. That count is the shell, and it is what cancels one of the two falloffs

premise
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)

a site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the sites at exactly r steps are those within r less those within r-1 - a subtraction, with nothing left over and nothing counted twice

sites within r steps = 8
cited
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD

established earlier by meeting.rate, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

the difference of a dilate
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)
= β·rD - β·(r-1)D
= β·rD - β·(rD - D·rD-1 + ...)
= β·D·rD-1 + ...
∝ β·rD-1

every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

multiplying
rate ∝ STEP·rD-1·rate(r)

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

definition
rate(r) = chance · chance'

a record is left where a charge from each source meets, so the rate at one place is what the first has put there times what the second has - both of which thinned on the way, and both of which are cited rather than counted again

multiplying
rate(r) ∝ chance·chance'

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

expansion
rate ∝ STEP·rD-1·chance·chance'

record here is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

a carrier is destroyed when it meets something. How far does ONE of them get before that happens?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
premise
death per step = partner · fatal fraction

ANNIHILATION is quantified over a facing pair and gated on "active", read off G itself rather than transcribed. So a carrier is destroyed on a step exactly when there is something facing it carrying something - which is how often partner - AND that meeting is one of the ones that leaves nothing - which is fatal fraction. Neither alone kills anything. ASSUMED HERE, and nowhere else: that whether a partner is present is not correlated with whether the carrier is, which is the standard kinetic assumption and is what lets the two be multiplied

rules that can destroy a carrier in flight = 1
a chance per step compounds
\lambda = -1/ln(1 - death per step)

and the length it dies over is that chance's own logarithm. This is a transcendental in a folder of counts, and deliberately so: death per step is a ratio of counts and its logarithm is not, but it is a CLOSED FORM which names exactly which counts it came from - which is what distinguishes it from a fitted parameter. A theory that destroys nothing has death per step = 0 and a range that is infinite, so its forces are not screened at all

a source emits gravity, and so does anything that turns. With no counting condition of any kind, what relation does that fix between a bound thing's mass and its size?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
mcloud = ∑r Mr = Mr · L

AND THE CLOUD IS ALL OF THOSE SHELLS ADDED UP. Since every shell weighs the same, the sum is that weight times HOW MANY SHELLS THERE ARE - so what the cloud comes to is set by HOW FAR IT REACHES and not by how the field falls off. That extent is what an energy state IS here: how fast the thing rotates and how far what it throws off gets before it is eaten. The mass ratio is therefore a question about L, and the falloff has cancelled itself out of it

definition
Mr = \omegar · shell

SO A WHOLE SHELL IS WHAT ONE CELL DOES TIMES HOW MANY CELLS THERE ARE, and this is where the two exponents meet: the field thins as r1-D and the room grows as rD-1, so THE PRODUCT DOES NOT DEPEND ON r AT ALL. Every shell of the cloud weighs the same, which is conservation said as an arithmetic - the rays that left the source are all still there, spread thinner over more room

definition
\omegar ∝ g

what one cell out there is doing is what the source's gravity comes to there, which is the first line again - a cell is turned as hard as the field at it

definition
shell = STEP·rD-1

AND THE VACUUM AROUND IT IS MANY MANY CELLS relative to the thing at the middle, which is the whole point: `lattice.shell-growth` counts the room at a distance as STEP·rD-1, and that count GROWS while the field thins

multiplying
Mr ∝ 1

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

summing over every shell
mcloud → ∞
mcloud = ∑∞r Mr
Mr ∝ 1
∑∞r r0 → ∞

Mr goes as 1, so in r it falls off as r0 - which is to say it does not fall off at all. Every shell contributes the same, and there is no end of shells. So the total does not converge

summing over every shell
mcloud → ∞
mcloud = ∑∞r Mr
Mr ∝ 1

Mr goes as 1, so in r it falls off as r0 - which is to say it does not fall off at all. Every shell contributes the same, and there is no end of shells. So the total does not converge

a source emits gravity, and so does anything that turns. With no counting condition of any kind, what relation does that fix between a bound thing's mass and its size?
G^XOR^o on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
mcloud = ∑r Mr = Mr · L

AND THE CLOUD IS ALL OF THOSE SHELLS ADDED UP. Since every shell weighs the same, the sum is that weight times HOW MANY SHELLS THERE ARE - so what the cloud comes to is set by HOW FAR IT REACHES and not by how the field falls off. That extent is what an energy state IS here: how fast the thing rotates and how far what it throws off gets before it is eaten. The mass ratio is therefore a question about L, and the falloff has cancelled itself out of it

definition
Mr = \omegar · shell

SO A WHOLE SHELL IS WHAT ONE CELL DOES TIMES HOW MANY CELLS THERE ARE, and this is where the two exponents meet: the field thins as r1-D and the room grows as rD-1, so THE PRODUCT DOES NOT DEPEND ON r AT ALL. Every shell of the cloud weighs the same, which is conservation said as an arithmetic - the rays that left the source are all still there, spread thinner over more room

charge is made in pairs and destroyed in pairs, what is left over is bent by everything inside it, and the bending itself weighs. What does a bound cloud come to, and how does it stand against the tightest thing that can close?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
dMdr = dMdr

and that is what dM/dr MEANS - the rate the enclosed mass grows at as the radius does. Naming it is not a premise about the world; it is saying which derivative the product above is

definition
dMdr = shell · \omega · f

AND WHAT THE NEXT SHELL ADDS IS ITS CELLS, TIMES WHAT EACH IS TURNING AT, TIMES WHAT SURVIVES THE CANCELLING. (G/2) makes charge in pairs and ANNIHILATION unmakes it in pairs, so what can act on anything is the residual, and f is that fraction - a property of the meeting rule, measured rather than assumed. THE THREE FACTORS ARE HANDED OVER SEPARATELY AND NOT MULTIPLIED HERE: what they come to is for the rules to work out, and the cancellation between the room and the falloff is the whole content of this theorem rather than something to be asserted in a sentence

definition
\omega = MSTEP·rD-1

WHAT BENDS A CELL IS EVERYTHING INSIDE IT. The second premise says turning emits gravity and `lib/Trajectory.ts` says mass IS turning, so the cloud that has already gathered is part of what does the bending - the field reads M and not the source alone. It spreads over the room above, which is the only geometry in this

multiplying
dMdr ∝ M·f·shellrD-1

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

a rate proportional to itself
MM0 = ef·r - 1

and what has ACCUMULATED is that less what it started from, so the ratio of the two is set by the single dimensionless product f·r and by nothing else at all - not by the dimension, not by the lattice, not by how far anything reaches on its own

a body sits r steps away from another in the medium. How does what it feels depend on r, and on what else?
G on square-4
definition
F = A · δ/site

what a body feels is what the medium has to offer where it stands, times how much of the medium it is open to. That is what a force IS in this model, and it mentions no distance

multiplying
F ∝ A·δ/site

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

premise
δ is conserved in flight

under EVERY rule of G, the difference between a perturbed world and an unperturbed one at the same seed, INTEGRATED over every site where they differ, SETTLES: over the second half of 16 ticks it trends 0.250 a tick, 1.3 sigma from flat against its own scatter, so it is not being made on the way. The count of rays cannot be the conserved thing - (G/2) makes them and (G/1) unmakes them - and neither can the footprint, which grows like the shell. What holds is what is spread over that footprint, which is the quantity the dilution above is about

the disturbance, integrated, tick by tick = 3; rules set aside to ask this = 0
premise
δ travels through ρ

under EVERY rule of G, the place a perturbed world and an unperturbed one differ spreads along the lattice's own exits - one exit a tick, watched as a front that never runs ahead of the steps it has taken. So a disturbance gets from here to there BY TRAVELLING THROUGH the medium, which is what makes the medium's own evenness a fact about the disturbance as well

how far the disturbance has reached, tick by tick = 16
premise
the lattice carries alike in every direction

the exit set's second moment is a multiple of the identity, so nothing carried on this lattice prefers a direction at second order

second moment anisotropy = 0.0000
carrying
δ goes every way alike

deficit travels through ρ, and ρ prefers no direction - so neither does what it carries

definition
δ ∝ S

the disturbance a body leaves is the rays it took out, and how many that is per tick is what S names. This is what the letter means, not something measured about it

spreading
δ/site ∝ Sshell

conserved and even, so one site's share is the whole of it over the number of sites there are at that distance

premise
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)

a site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the sites at exactly r steps are those within r less those within r-1 - a subtraction, with nothing left over and nothing counted twice

sites within r steps = 8
premise
ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
ball(r) = 1, 5, 13, 25, 41, 61, 85, 113, 145
Δ1 = 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32
Δ2 = 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4

the sites within r steps are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step - take one step r times and you are somewhere in r·P, and every site of r·P is reached that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 2, which is D, exactly and on integers

sites within r steps = 8; degree of the count in r = 2
Ehrhart's theorem
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD
ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
= β·rD + c1·rD-1 + ... + cD
∝ β·rD

Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality

the difference of a dilate
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)
= β·rD - β·(r-1)D
= β·rD - β·(rD - D·rD-1 + ...)
= β·D·rD-1 + ...
∝ β·rD-1

every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

expansion
δ/site ∝ SSTEP·rD-1

shell is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

cited
S = A'

established earlier by vacuum.suppression, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

which is also a scaling
S ∝ A'

S is A', which is a single product of powers - so it scales as that, and whatever was written in terms of S can be written in terms of what it is made of

expansion
δ/site ∝ A'STEP·rD-1

S is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

expansion
F ∝ A·A'STEP·rD-1

n[deficit] is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

a body sits r steps away from another in the medium. How does what it feels depend on r, and on what else?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6
definition
F = A · δ/site

what a body feels is what the medium has to offer where it stands, times how much of the medium it is open to. That is what a force IS in this model, and it mentions no distance

multiplying
F ∝ A·δ/site

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

G^XOR*2 on fcc-12, cubic-6
definition
F = A · δ/site

what a body feels is what the medium has to offer where it stands, times how much of the medium it is open to. That is what a force IS in this model, and it mentions no distance

multiplying

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

premise
δ is conserved in flight

under EVERY rule of GXOR*2, the difference between a perturbed world and an unperturbed one at the same seed, INTEGRATED over every site where they differ, SETTLES: over the second half of 16 ticks it trends -4.250 a tick, 0.6 sigma from flat against its own scatter, so it is not being made on the way. The count of rays cannot be the conserved thing - (G/2) makes them and (G/1) unmakes them - and neither can the footprint, which grows like the shell. What holds is what is spread over that footprint, which is the quantity the dilution above is about

the disturbance, integrated, tick by tick = 13; rules set aside to ask this = 0
premise
δ travels through ρ

under EVERY rule of GXOR*2, the place a perturbed world and an unperturbed one differ spreads along the lattice's own exits - one exit a tick, watched as a front that never runs ahead of the steps it has taken. So a disturbance gets from here to there BY TRAVELLING THROUGH the medium, which is what makes the medium's own evenness a fact about the disturbance as well

how far the disturbance has reached, tick by tick = 16
premise
the lattice carries alike in every direction

the exit set's second moment is a multiple of the identity, so nothing carried on this lattice prefers a direction at second order

second moment anisotropy = 0.0000
carrying
δ goes every way alike

deficit travels through ρ, and ρ prefers no direction - so neither does what it carries

what a body feels is what the medium has to offer where it stands, times how much of the medium it is open to. That is what a force IS in this model, and it mentions no distance

multiplying
F ∝ A·δ/site

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

a body sits r steps away from another in the medium. How does what it feels depend on r, and on what else?
G^XOR · relaxing(2/1) on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4
definition
F = A · δ/site

what a body feels is what the medium has to offer where it stands, times how much of the medium it is open to. That is what a force IS in this model, and it mentions no distance

multiplying
F ∝ A·δ/site

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

put the pieces together. What is the gravitational force between two bodies R apart, with every factor written in?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
Fg = Fmeet + Fvac

what a body feels is everything that arrives at it, and things that arrive add. So the gravitational force is the two channels together: the meetings between the bodies' own radiation, and the expansion the vacuum did not manage around them

definition
Fmeet = lean · share · SHEET2 · m · m' · met(R)

what arrives through MEETINGS is what a meeting is worth to a path, times how much of the time the two phases are opposed, times the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, times the two masses, times the meetings summed along the line between them. Every one of those was proved somewhere else and is cited; this line only says how they multiply

substituting
Fg = Fvac + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fg = Fmeet + Fvac
Fmeet = SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fg = Fvac + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share

Fmeet is not a primitive of this theory - it is SHEET2·lean·ma·mb·met(R)·share, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
Fvac = A⊥ · SSTEP·R-D+1

and what arrives because the vacuum's expansion was SUPPRESSED is the other channel. A body's cells are not neutral, so the split does not fire on them; the expansion that did not happen there spreads outward and a second body is pushed into the shortfall. This needs neither body to emit anything - an inert absorber has it - which is what makes it a separate arrival rather than the meeting term counted again. It thins as the dense regime says, because the deficit is carried by the same rays as everything else. Note the two areas are not the same kind of area: what the near body SENDS leaves through the whole of its boundary and spreads isotropically, so its full A' counts; what the far body FEELS is an imbalance along the line between them, so only its facing cross-section takes part

cited
S = A'

established earlier by vacuum.suppression, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

substituting
Fvac = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP
Fvac = A⊥·SRD-1·STEP
S = A'
Fvac = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP

S is not a primitive of this theory - it is A', so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

substituting
Fg = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fg = Fvac + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fvac = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP
Fg = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share

Fvac is not a primitive of this theory - it is A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

cited
lean = cDEG

established earlier by lattice.lean, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

substituting
Fg = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·c·m·m'·met(R)·shareDEG
Fg = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
lean = cDEG
Fg = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·c·m·m'·met(R)·shareDEG

lean is not a primitive of this theory - it is cDEG, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

over a common denominator
Fg = num(Fg)den(Fg)

so Fg is the one over the other

over a common denominator
num(Fg) = A'·A⊥·DEGRD-1 + SHEET2·STEP·c·m·m'·met(R)·share

putting Fg over DEG·STEP, what is left on top is A'·A⊥·DEGRD-1 + SHEET2·STEP·c·ma·mb·met(R)·share - the schoolbook move, and nothing about it knows what these quantities are

over a common denominator
den(Fg) = DEG·STEP

and underneath is DEG·STEP

one over another
Fg = A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·c·ln(R/c)·m·m'DEG·RD + 2·SHEET2·m·m'DEG·RD-1·cD-3
Fg = num(Fg) / den(Fg)
= (A'·A⊥·DEGRD-1 + SHEET2·STEP·c·m·m'·met(R)·share) / (DEG·STEP)
= A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·c·ln(R/c)·m·m'DEG·RD + 2·SHEET2·m·m'DEG·RD-1·cD-3

num(Fg) is A'·A⊥·DEGRD-1 + SHEET2·STEP·c·ma·mb·met(R)·share and den(Fg) is DEG·STEP, so the one over the other is A'·A⊥RD-1·STEP + SHEET2·c·ln(R/c)·ma·mbDEG·RD + 2·SHEET2·ma·mbDEG·RD-1·cD-3

what arrives through MEETINGS is what a meeting is worth to a path, times how much of the time the two phases are opposed, times the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, times the two masses, times the meetings summed along the line between them. Every one of those was proved somewhere else and is cited; this line only says how they multiply

substituting
Fg = Fvac + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fg = Fmeet + Fvac
Fmeet = SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fg = Fvac + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share

Fmeet is not a primitive of this theory - it is SHEET2·lean·ma·mb·met(R)·share, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
Fvac = A⊥ · SSTEP·R(-D+1)/2

and what arrives because the vacuum's expansion was SUPPRESSED is the other channel. A body's cells are not neutral, so the split does not fire on them; the expansion that did not happen there spreads outward and a second body is pushed into the shortfall. This needs neither body to emit anything - an inert absorber has it - which is what makes it a separate arrival rather than the meeting term counted again. It thins as the thin regime says, because the deficit is carried by the same rays as everything else. Note the two areas are not the same kind of area: what the near body SENDS leaves through the whole of its boundary and spreads isotropically, so its full A' counts; what the far body FEELS is an imbalance along the line between them, so only its facing cross-section takes part

cited
S = A'

established earlier by vacuum.suppression, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

substituting
Fvac = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP
Fvac = A⊥·SR(D-1)/2·STEP
S = A'
Fvac = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP

S is not a primitive of this theory - it is A', so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

substituting
Fg = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fg = Fvac + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
Fvac = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP
Fg = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share

Fvac is not a primitive of this theory - it is A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

established earlier by lattice.lean, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

substituting
Fg = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP + SHEET2·c·m·m'·met(R)·shareDEG
Fg = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP + SHEET2·lean·m·m'·met(R)·share
lean = cDEG

lean is not a primitive of this theory - it is cDEG, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

over a common denominator
Fg = num(Fg)den(Fg)

so Fg is the one over the other

over a common denominator
num(Fg) = A'·A⊥·DEGR(D-1)/2 + SHEET2·STEP·c·m·m'·met(R)·share

putting Fg over DEG·STEP, what is left on top is A'·A⊥·DEGR(D-1)/2 + SHEET2·STEP·c·ma·mb·met(R)·share - the schoolbook move, and nothing about it knows what these quantities are

over a common denominator
den(Fg) = DEG·STEP

and underneath is DEG·STEP

one over another
Fg = A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP + 1/2·SHEET2·c·ln(R/c)·m·m'DEG·R(D+1)/2 + SHEET2·m·m'DEG·R(D-1)/2·c(D-5)/2
Fg = num(Fg) / den(Fg)
= (A'·A⊥·DEGR(D-1)/2 + SHEET2·STEP·c·m·m'·met(R)·share) / (DEG·STEP)
= A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP + 1/2·SHEET2·c·ln(R/c)·m·m'DEG·R(D+1)/2 + SHEET2·m·m'DEG·R(D-1)/2·c(D-5)/2

num(Fg) is A'·A⊥·DEGR(D-1)/2 + SHEET2·STEP·c·ma·mb·met(R)·share and den(Fg) is DEG·STEP, so the one over the other is A'·A⊥R(D-1)/2·STEP + 1/2·SHEET2·c·ln(R/c)·ma·mbDEG·R(D+1)/2 + SHEET2·ma·mbDEG·R(D-1)/2·c(D-5)/2

and what arrives because the vacuum's expansion was SUPPRESSED is the other channel. A body's cells are not neutral, so the split does not fire on them; the expansion that did not happen there spreads outward and a second body is pushed into the shortfall. This needs neither body to emit anything - an inert absorber has it - which is what makes it a separate arrival rather than the meeting term counted again. It thins as the dense regime says, because the deficit is carried by the same rays as everything else. Note the two areas are not the same kind of area: what the near body SENDS leaves through the whole of its boundary and spreads isotropically, so its full A' counts; what the far body FEELS is an imbalance along the line between them, so only its facing cross-section takes part

cited
S = A'

S is not a primitive of this theory - it is A', so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

the shortfall around a body grows without limit as you approach it, and a point has only so many exits to be missing. What happens where they meet?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
premise
what gets out = 0

at the ceiling every one of a point's 12 exits is dark. Leaving is what an exit is, so nothing leaves such a point by any route - not a weakened signal, none. That is a horizon in the only sense this model has one, and it is not put in anywhere: it is where a law that has to keep growing meets a count that cannot

DEG = 12

a source emits gravity, turning emits gravity, and the axis can only wind a whole number of ring steps a beat. With no wavelength and no counting condition put on the electron, where do the shells stand and what does it cost to leave one?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
En ∝ \omegan2

AND WHAT IT COSTS TO LEAVE IS THE TURNING TWICE OVER. Mass is the rate of bending - `gravity.atom`'s premise - and what a thing at that rate carries goes as the rate again, so the energy is quadratic in ω. Nothing about this is put in for the atom; it is the same statement `mass.budget` makes when it writes β2

definition
\omegan ∝ 1rn

EVERYTHING MOVES AT ONE CELL A TICK, so a closed curve of radius r is 2πr cells round and a lap is CYCLE ring steps - `GXORo`'s own `laps`. Holding that curve therefore costs CYCLE/(2πr) ring steps a tick, and neither π nor CYCLE depends on which curve is being asked about. This is `gravity.atom`'s second line and it is cited rather than re-argued

multiplying
En ∝ 1rn2

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

Nothing about this is put in for the atom; it is the same statement `mass.budget` makes when it writes β2

EVERYTHING MOVES AT ONE CELL A TICK, so a closed curve of radius r is 2πr cells round and a lap is CYCLE ring steps - `GXORo`'s own `laps`. Holding that curve therefore costs CYCLE/(2πr) ring steps a tick, and neither π nor CYCLE depends on which curve is being asked about. This is `gravity.atom`'s second line and it is cited rather than re-argued

definition
share* = 1

the half in share.coherence came from averaging |ψ|/π over a phase difference that was anybody's guess. Two of the same thing pulse at the same rate, so their phase difference is not anybody's guess - there is nothing left to average, and what would have been averaged down is not

which is a number
share* = 1

1 has nothing left in it that varies, so it is 1 exactly

the retarded force and the metric both correct gravity for motion. Are those two effects, one effect twice, or one of them short of something?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
missing = kmetric - kretard

so what the retarded route does not account for is the difference, and it is B's term less the clock convention. THE GAP IS NOT A DISAGREEMENT BUT A MISSING TERM: the retarded force is the metric with the space part left out. That is why the two are compared rather than multiplied - multiplying would count A twice and still never mention B

definition
kretard = kA + 1/2

the retarded force carries A's beta2 - its two branches and its clock are exactly what a late arrival and a slow clock do - plus a half from whose clock the answer is quoted per, which this folder makes a switch of. That is 3/2 on the receiver's clock and 1 on the lattice's

definition
kA = 1

splitting the Hamiltonian's radial force in the counted metric, the piece coming from the time part A carries 1.00 beta2 - measured at r = 104, where the static term is six parts in ten thousand and does not confuse the reading. This is the part a slow clock and a delayed arrival account for

substituting
kretard = 3/2
kretard = 1/2 + kA
kA = 1
kretard = 3/2

kA is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

substituting
missing = -3/2 + kmetric
missing = kmetric - kretard
kretard = 3/2
missing = -3/2 + kmetric

kretard is not a primitive of this theory - it is 3/2, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
kmetric = kA + kB

so the metric's whole velocity correction is the two together, 2 beta2 - which is what differentiating it gives directly, so the split accounts for all of it

substituting
kmetric = 1 + kB
kmetric = kA + kB
kA = 1
kmetric = 1 + kB

kA is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
kB = 1

and the piece from the space part B carries another 1.00 beta2. This is space being stretched where the count is high, which is not a statement about when anything arrives - so nothing about travel time can produce it

substituting
kmetric = 2
kmetric = 1 + kB
kB = 1
kmetric = 2

kB is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

substituting
missing = 1/2
missing = -3/2 + kmetric
kmetric = 2
missing = 1/2

kmetric is not a primitive of this theory - it is 2, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

which is a number
missing = 1/2

1/2 has nothing left in it that varies, so it is 1/2 exactly

n annihilations have happened at a place. How much does a path through it lean, and does that stop growing?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
lean1 = n · cDEG

an annihilation gives the direction it went one extra way of being taken, so after n of them that direction has 1 + n ways against the 1 each that the DEG alternatives still have. The surplus is n, each worth a step, against DEG - and a path's lean is that. Note what is NOT here: nothing divides by anything that grows with n, so the lean is linear in the count and has no ceiling

the lean threw away how many ways out there now are. Read that way instead, what does the same count give?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
δ = B3/2 - 1

the correction is what the path accumulates over and above flat space, which is that quantity less one

definition
B3/2 = B3/2

what a path accumulates through the stretched space goes as B to the three halves - and three halves is not a number of times you can multiply something by itself, so the next line is a series rather than a product

definition
B = 1 + 2u

the ways out of the point number DEG + n rather than DEG, which over DEG is 1 + n/DEG - the same everywhere, so one number per place and no tensor needed. Written in the potential that is 1 + 2u, which is what u NAMES; the factor of two is the normalisation the article carries, not a step

the binomial series
B3/2 = 1 + 3·u
B = 1 + 2·u
B3/2 = (1 + 2·u)3/2
= 1 + 3/2·2·u + ... (to order 1)
= 1 + 3·u

B is 1 + 2·u, which is one plus 2·u. Raised to 3/2 that is the binomial theorem in 2·u, kept to order 1

substituting
δ = 3·u
δ = -1 + B3/2
B3/2 = 1 + 3·u
δ = 3·u

B3/2 is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 + 3·u, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

mass goes as one over size, so a mass ratio is a size ratio. What are the two sizes a bound pair has here, and what does the ratio between them come to?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
mpme = rerp = 2\pi·\lambdaCYCLE

AND A MASS RATIO IS A SIZE RATIO INVERTED, which is `gravity.atom`'s m ∝ 1/r and nothing more. Both masses are the same kind of thing - an amount of turning - so the constant between mass and size is the same for both and cancels. What is left is 2πλ/CYCLE, and every symbol in it is a count this folder already derives

definition
rp = CYCLE2\pi

THE TIGHTEST THING THAT CAN CLOSE is a lap, and a lap is CYCLE ring steps - `GXORo`'s `laps`, and `lattice.turn` establishes that CYCLE does not grow with the dimension. A closed curve whose circumference is CYCLE cells has radius CYCLE/(2π), and nothing smaller closes because there is no shorter way round the ring. The 2π is not fitted; it is what a circumference is

expansion
mpme ∝ reCYCLE

rp is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

definition
re = \lambda

AND THE CLOUD REACHES AS FAR AS ITS CARRIERS DO. `gravity.atom` establishes that every shell of it weighs the same, so its mass is set by HOW MANY SHELLS there are and diverges without a cut - and what cuts it is the carrier being eaten, which `reach.range` derives from the vacuum's occupancy rather than assuming

which is also a scaling
re ∝ \lambda

re is \lambda, which is a single product of powers - so it scales as that, and whatever was written in terms of re can be written in terms of what it is made of

expansion
mpme ∝ \lambdaCYCLE

re is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

premise
death per step = partner · fatal fraction

ANNIHILATION is quantified over a facing pair and gated on "active", read off G itself rather than transcribed. So a carrier is destroyed on a step exactly when there is something facing it carrying something - which is how often partner - AND that meeting is one of the ones that leaves nothing - which is fatal fraction. Neither alone kills anything. ASSUMED HERE, and nowhere else: that whether a partner is present is not correlated with whether the carrier is, which is the standard kinetic assumption and is what lets the two be multiplied

rules that can destroy a carrier in flight = 1
a chance per step compounds
\lambda = -1/ln(1 - death per step)

and the length it dies over is that chance's own logarithm. This is a transcendental in a folder of counts, and deliberately so: death per step is a ratio of counts and its logarithm is not, but it is a CLOSED FORM which names exactly which counts it came from - which is what distinguishes it from a fitted parameter. A theory that destroys nothing has death per step = 0 and a range that is infinite, so its forces are not screened at all

every source in the universe is putting charges everywhere. Adding up what all of them put on you, is there a total?
G on square-4
definition
Φ = ∑r dΦ

every source in the universe is putting charges everywhere, so what arrives at you is what all of them put together - taken shell by shell, out as far as there are shells

definition
dΦ = M(r) · δ/site

what one shell puts on you is how much matter is in it, times what a unit of matter at that distance puts on you - and the second of those is the falloff, cited rather than reproved

definition
M(r) ∝ ρ · shell

a shell at r steps has as many sites in it as the shell has, and matter is spread through space at some density - so the matter it holds is the one times the other. No power appears here; the shell's size is established separately

cited
δ/site ∝ A'STEP·rD-1

established earlier by gravity.falloff, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

multiplying
dΦ ∝ A'·shell·ρSTEP·rD-1

each factor carries its own dependence and they multiply

premise
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)

a site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the sites at exactly r steps are those within r less those within r-1 - a subtraction, with nothing left over and nothing counted twice

sites within r steps = 8
cited
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD

established earlier by gravity.falloff, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

the difference of a dilate
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)
= β·rD - β·(r-1)D
= β·rD - β·(rD - D·rD-1 + ...)
= β·D·rD-1 + ...
∝ β·rD-1

every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

expansion
dΦ ∝ A'·ρ

shell is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here

summing over every shell
Φ → ∞
Φ = ∑∞r dΦ
dΦ ∝ A'·ρ
∑∞r r0 → ∞

what the shell puts on you goes as A'·ρm, so in r it falls off as r0 - which is to say it does not fall off at all. Every shell contributes the same, and there is no end of shells. So the total does not converge

nothing here acts at a distance - a shortfall crosses one cell a tick. What does that do to the gravitational law when the two bodies are moving?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
Fgrel = Fg · retardation · γmr-ms

so the force is the one between bodies at rest, times what retardation does to what arrives, times gamma to whatever power the clocks call for. k is +1 if the answer is counted in the receiver's own ticks and -1 if the source is the one moving - a numerator reduction, since a slowed source pulses less often - and 0 in the lattice's own frame, which is where the dynamics run

premise
γ = (1-β2)-1/2

the clock advances by the crossing component, which is the root of that - so a moving thing ticks at sqrt(1 - β2) and one lattice tick is worth (1 - β2)-1/2 of its own. The Lorentz factor, out of a step of fixed length and nothing else

distinct exit lengths = 1
kept exact
γ = (1-β2)-1/2

γ is (1-β2) to the -1/2, and it is carried as that rather than expanded. The exponent is not a whole positive number, so a series would be infinite and would have to be cut somewhere - and anything built on the cut version inherits the cut. Kept closed it is exact

substituting
Fgrel = Fg·retardation(1-β2)(mr-ms)/2
Fgrel = Fg·retardation·γmr-ms
γ = 1(1-β2)1/2
Fgrel = Fg·retardation(1-β2)(mr-ms)/2

γ is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1-β2)1/2, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
retardation = w·ahead + (1-w)·behind

how much of the time you are on each side is w and 1 - w, so what arrives is the two branches at those weights. Ignorance is w = 1/2 and is not a special case of anything - it is the value that makes the two equal. What this average COMES to is not stated here: it is put over a common denominator by the rules below, and what falls out is exact

definition
ahead = 1(1-β)

what arrives from the compressed branch goes as one over that - carried as an exact power rather than expanded, so nothing below inherits a truncation

kept exact
ahead = (1-β)-1

ahead is (1-β) to the -1, and it is carried as that rather than expanded. The exponent is not a whole positive number, so a series would be infinite and would have to be cut somewhere - and anything built on the cut version inherits the cut. Kept closed it is exact

substituting
retardation = w(1-β) + behind - behind·w
retardation = ahead·w + behind - behind·w
ahead = 1(1-β)
retardation = w(1-β) + behind - behind·w

ahead is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1-β), so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
behind = 1(1+β)

and from the stretched one, one over the other

kept exact
behind = (1+β)-1

behind is (1+β) to the -1, and it is carried as that rather than expanded. The exponent is not a whole positive number, so a series would be infinite and would have to be cut somewhere - and anything built on the cut version inherits the cut. Kept closed it is exact

substituting
retardation = w(1-β) + 1(1+β) - w(1+β)
retardation = w(1-β) + behind - behind·w
behind = 1(1+β)
retardation = w(1-β) + 1(1+β) - w(1+β)

behind is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1+β), so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

over a common denominator
retardation = num(retardation)den(retardation)

so retardation is the one over the other

over a common denominator
num(retardation) = (1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w

putting retardation over (1+β)·(1-β), what is left on top is (1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w - the schoolbook move, and nothing about it knows what these quantities are

over a common denominator
den(retardation) = (1+β)·(1-β)

and underneath is (1+β)·(1-β)

definition
(1-β) = 1 - β

over the delay the source has moved, so the branch that set out ahead of the motion left from closer than R and arrives compressed - by one less the fraction of a cell a tick it is going

substituting
den(retardation) = (1+β) - (1+β)·β
den(retardation) = (1+β)·(1-β)
(1-β) = 1 - β
den(retardation) = (1+β) - (1+β)·β

(1-β) is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 - β, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

the same quantity
den(retardation) = (1-β2)

den(retardation) and (1-β2) both come to 1 - β2, so they are the same quantity reached by two roads - and whatever is written in terms of one can be written in terms of the other

one over another
retardation = 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)
retardation = num(retardation) / den(retardation)
= ((1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w) / ((1-β2))
= 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)

num(retardation) is (1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w and den(retardation) is (1-β2), so the one over the other is 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)

substituting
Fgrel = Fg(1-β2)(mr-ms+2)/2 + Fg·cos(θ)·β(1-β2)(mr-ms+2)/2
Fgrel = Fg·retardation(1-β2)(mr-ms)/2
retardation = 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)
Fgrel = Fg(1-β2)(mr-ms+2)/2 + Fg·cos(θ)·β(1-β2)(mr-ms+2)/2

retardation is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2), so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

γ = (1-β2)-1/2

γ is (1-β2) to the -1/2, and it is carried as that rather than expanded. The exponent is not a whole positive number, so a series would be infinite and would have to be cut somewhere - and anything built on the cut version inherits the cut. Kept closed it is exact

substituting
Fgrel = Fg·retardation(1-β2)(mr-ms)/2
Fgrel = Fg·retardation·γmr-ms
γ = 1(1-β2)1/2
Fgrel = Fg·retardation(1-β2)(mr-ms)/2

γ is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1-β2)1/2, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
retardation = w·ahead + (1-w)·behind

how much of the time you are on each side is w and 1 - w, so what arrives is the two branches at those weights. Ignorance is w = 1/2 and is not a special case of anything - it is the value that makes the two equal. What this average COMES to is not stated here: it is put over a common denominator by the rules below, and what falls out is exact

definition
ahead = 1(1-β)

what arrives from the compressed branch goes as one over that - carried as an exact power rather than expanded, so nothing below inherits a truncation

kept exact
ahead = (1-β)-1

ahead is (1-β) to the -1, and it is carried as that rather than expanded. The exponent is not a whole positive number, so a series would be infinite and would have to be cut somewhere - and anything built on the cut version inherits the cut. Kept closed it is exact

substituting
retardation = w(1-β) + behind - behind·w
retardation = ahead·w + behind - behind·w
ahead = 1(1-β)
retardation = w(1-β) + behind - behind·w

ahead is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1-β), so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
behind = 1(1+β)

and from the stretched one, one over the other

kept exact
behind = (1+β)-1

behind is (1+β) to the -1, and it is carried as that rather than expanded. The exponent is not a whole positive number, so a series would be infinite and would have to be cut somewhere - and anything built on the cut version inherits the cut. Kept closed it is exact

substituting
retardation = w(1-β) + 1(1+β) - w(1+β)
retardation = w(1-β) + behind - behind·w
behind = 1(1+β)
retardation = w(1-β) + 1(1+β) - w(1+β)

behind is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1+β), so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

over a common denominator
retardation = num(retardation)den(retardation)

so retardation is the one over the other

over a common denominator
num(retardation) = (1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w

putting retardation over (1+β)·(1-β), what is left on top is (1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w - the schoolbook move, and nothing about it knows what these quantities are

over a common denominator
den(retardation) = (1+β)·(1-β)

and underneath is (1+β)·(1-β)

definition
(1-β) = 1 - β

over the delay the source has moved, so the branch that set out ahead of the motion left from closer than R and arrives compressed - by one less the fraction of a cell a tick it is going

substituting
den(retardation) = (1+β) - (1+β)·β
den(retardation) = (1+β)·(1-β)
(1-β) = 1 - β
den(retardation) = (1+β) - (1+β)·β

(1-β) is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 - β, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

the same quantity
den(retardation) = (1-β2)

den(retardation) and (1-β2) both come to 1 - β2, so they are the same quantity reached by two roads - and whatever is written in terms of one can be written in terms of the other

one over another
retardation = 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)
retardation = num(retardation) / den(retardation)
= ((1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w) / ((1-β2))
= 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)

num(retardation) is (1-β) - (1-β)·w + (1+β)·w and den(retardation) is (1-β2), so the one over the other is 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)

substituting
Fgrel = Fg(1-β2)(mr-ms+2)/2 + Fg·cos(θ)·β(1-β2)(mr-ms+2)/2

retardation = 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2)

retardation is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1-β2) + cos(θ)·β(1-β2), so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
Fgrel = Fg · retardation · γmr-ms

so the force is the one between bodies at rest, times what retardation does to what arrives, times gamma to whatever power the clocks call for. k is +1 if the answer is counted in the receiver's own ticks and -1 if the source is the one moving - a numerator reduction, since a slowed source pulses less often - and 0 in the lattice's own frame, which is where the dynamics run

the lean and the stretch are two readings of one count. Put together, what metric do they make - and does it move a perihelion the way general relativity does?
G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
A·B = A · B

the metric is ds² = -A dt² + B dr², so what there is to ask about the two together is their product. Multiplied out it is (1 - 2u)(1 + 2u) = 1 - 4u², which is one to this order - the two readings are INVERSES. That is what Schwarzschild has in isotropic form, and it is not put in here: it follows from both being readings of one count, so what the count does to the ways through a point it does inversely to the ways round it

definition
A = 1 - 2u

the lean makes a clock run slow where the count is high - that is the first reading, the one gravity.law takes, and in the potential it is 1 - 2u. The factor of two is the normalisation u carries, not a step

substituting
A·B = B - 2·B·u
A·B = A·B
A = 1 - 2·u
A·B = B - 2·B·u

A is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 - 2·u, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

cited
B = 1 + 2u

established earlier by gravity.metric, on this same theory and lattice - the working is there rather than repeated here

substituting
A·B = 1 - 4·u2
A·B = B - 2·B·u
B = 1 + 2·u
A·B = 1 - 4·u2

B is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 + 2·u, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
u << 1

the potential is small wherever this is asked - far outside anything dense - so its square is smaller still and the first order is the whole of it

to first order
A·B = 1
A·B = 1 - 4·u2
u << 1
A·B = 1

u is much smaller than one, so powers of it beyond the first are smaller still and are dropped. What is kept is everything to first order in it - stated rather than assumed, and the line above is what it was before

which is a number
A·B = 1

1 has nothing left in it that varies, so it is 1 exactly

what is one annihilation worth to a path, on this lattice?
G on fcc-12
definition
lean = cDEG

an annihilation gives the direction it went one extra way of being taken, while every other way out of that point still weighs exactly what it did before - and there are DEG of those. So the lean is a step against DEG: what the annihilation bought, over the alternatives it did not take. The numerator is c rather than a bare 1 because what it bought is a step, and a step is c

premise
c = 1

a step's worth of lean is what one annihilation buys a path, and a step is c - one cell a tick, the lattice's own speed. Its value in those units is one, which is a statement about the units and not about the quantity. A count of the tiling, taken off the geometry itself with nothing run and nothing fitted

c = 1
premise
DEG = 12

the ways out of a point on fcc-12 - the exits it has, counted. A count of the tiling, taken off the geometry itself with nothing run and nothing fitted

DEG = 12
a ratio of counts
lean = cDEG = 1/12
lean = cDEG
= 112
= 1/12

c is 1 and DEG is 12, both counted off the tiling, so the ratio is 1/12 exactly - and it is worth reading as c/DEG rather than as the number, because on another lattice it is a different number and the same ratio

premise
DEG = 12

the ways out of a point on fcc-12 - the exits it has, counted. A count of the tiling, taken off the geometry itself with nothing run and nothing fitted

DEG = 12
a ratio of counts

lean = cDEG
= 112
= 1/12

c is 1 and DEG is 12, both counted off the tiling, so the ratio is 1/12 exactly - and it is worth reading as c/DEG rather than as the number, because on another lattice it is a different number and the same ratio

what is one annihilation worth to a path, on this lattice?
G^XOR on cubic-6
definition
lean = cDEG

an annihilation gives the direction it went one extra way of being taken, while every other way out of that point still weighs exactly what it did before - and there are DEG of those. So the lean is a step against DEG: what the annihilation bought, over the alternatives it did not take. The numerator is c rather than a bare 1 because what it bought is a step, and a step is c

and what is left of the step after that divides again - LINEARLY. Every bend a ray makes happens at a point, and `blocks` sorts points into two kinds and no more: holding something, or not. That is a predicate, so the two are DISJOINT EVENTS partitioning an amount rather than orthogonal components resolving a vector. Amounts add; only vectors go in quadrature. Motion lost in the open is inertia and motion lost where matter is holding is what does the holding, and between them they are the whole of it

AND THE MASS IS WHAT THOSE TWO LEAVE. Not a definition of mass and not a measurement of one: the step is spent, the parts are named by which branch of which rule they fall on, and m is the one that is not held. MORE BINDING IS LESS MASS - the mass defect, and here it is the same subtraction rather than an analogy, because motion that has gone into holding a thing together is motion that is not available to weigh it

G on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
definition
p·r = p · r

and the two are multiplied here rather than at the end, so that a reader can watch what cancels. The momentum carries gamma·v and the node spacing carries its reciprocal - that is the same gamma and the same v, because the emitter whose phase makes the nodes is the thing whose momentum is being counted. So they go, and what is left has neither a speed nor a Lorentz factor in it, which is why this holds at any speed rather than only at a slow one

definition
p = \hbar\lambda·\gamma·v

and momentum is gamma·m·v. This model measures a mass as a wavelength - lbar is hbar/(m·c), which is what `mass.period` divides the budget by - so m is hbar/(lbar·c) and p is gamma·v·hbar/lbar at c = 1. A unit conversion and nothing else: there is no claim in this line that is not already in the definition of lbar

substituting
p·r = \gamma·\hbar·r·v\lambda
p·r = p·r
p = \gamma·\hbar·v\lambda
p·r = \gamma·\hbar·r·v\lambda

p is not a primitive of this theory - it is \gamma·\hbar·v\lambda, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

definition
r = n · \lambdadB/2

the nodes are a fixed distance apart, so how many of them a region holds is the region divided by that distance - and a region holding n of them is n of them long. THE ONLY PHYSICS IN THIS LINE IS THAT n IS A WHOLE NUMBER, and that is not a quantisation postulate: a node is a place where the emitter's two branches cancel, and there is no such thing as most of one

premise
\lambdadB/2 = \pi·\lambda\gamma·v

a place is reached by two rays from one emitter - the one that set out ahead of it and the one behind - and the two beat. The SUM of their phases carries the envelope, and the spacing between its nodes is what a standing wave is counted in. Measured by building the phase field and bracketing successive turns of 2·pi, at four speeds over three decades, it is pi·lbar/(gamma·v) to 9.6e-14. AT REST IT IS INFINITE - the sum stops depending on position at all - so motion is what makes a pattern, which is the shape a length that depends on momentum has to have

worst light-cone residual = 0.0000; variation of the phase SUM across 80 cells, at rest = 0; worst |envelope period / (pi·lbar/(gamma·v)) - 1| = 0.0000

r = \lambda·\pi·n\gamma·v
r = \lambdadB/2·n
\lambdadB/2 = \lambda·\pi\gamma·v
r = \lambda·\pi·n\gamma·v

\lambdadB/2 is not a primitive of this theory - it is \lambda·\pi\gamma·v, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

a source alternates its sign and its rays leave one cell a tick. What does the spacing between sign reversals say about how fast it is going?
G^XOR on fcc-12, cubic-6, square-4, line-2
premise
\delta · \hat{n} = c - \lambda(\hat{n})pulse period

read the other way round, the spacing between sign reversals at a place GIVES the component of the source's velocity along the line to it. That is a local reading - one place, one period, and no need to know which source it came from - and it is the velocity the source ACTUALLY has, because it is the displacement that shifted the fronts. So the emitter's velocity is already written into the phase pattern by rules that were there for other reasons, and a tag carrying a declared one adds no information. It is the declared number that is the weaker of the two: nothing in the dynamics sets it and nothing checks it against where the source goes
